### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 78ab6474ca30bbb7c4400bae548c814da8fa57c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3eb3e6c98b5a68075780fe8b80969f50ad9e3808` — the merge of head `e41097d2334238f2bf3827241b19a89a6eaa5b11` into base `78ab6474ca30bbb7c4400bae548c814da8fa57c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3eb3e6c98b5a68075780fe8b80969f50ad9e3808 && git checkout 3eb3e6c98b5a68075780fe8b80969f50ad9e3808
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 78ab6474ca30bbb7c4400bae548c814da8fa57c1 e41097d2334238f2bf3827241b19a89a6eaa5b11 && git checkout -B drift-repro 78ab6474ca30bbb7c4400bae548c814da8fa57c1 && git merge --no-ff e41097d2334238f2bf3827241b19a89a6eaa5b11

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 78ab6474ca30bbb7c4400bae548c814da8fa57c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 78ab6474ca30bbb7c4400bae548c814da8fa57c1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #24757 (its 18.x half) · `domain:services` seat 2 · `os-support-ai` · `session_01UmqzD97e14iws6hmVhgZ5y` · 2026-10-20T22:23Z · head `e41097d233`. This is the review of record for claim `6301409060`. Contract review: not owed. The PR touches no published schema and no governed path, and it declares `Clause-②: no` with no narrowing arm.

1. **Form:**
   - The first line is `Part of #24757`: the fold's retirement is the card's 19.0 half, so the card stays open. The seat's grep of the body finds no closing keyword beside any issue number, and `check-partof-closing-keyword` passed on the body.
   - `Clause-②: no` is at line start in the body and in the `plugin-security` changeset (`patch`), with its reason.
   - 3 files, +170/−53.
   - Path face, read with the files endpoint on this head: `check-governed-merges --pr 24988` reports 0 of 3 paths governed. Ordinary queue landing.
2. **Premise and fix:**
   - 「甲」 (#6015 `6292005854`) with triage's derivation for this card (`6292072572`): 18.x ships the existing warning, re-pointed as the loud half, and the grant does not change.
   - The `position_name_fold_grant` text now states that the set is in force only because the names match, that this name-based grant is removed in the next major version and what holders lose then, and the fix (`permissionSets: ['P']`, or a rename).
   - The payload gains `removedIn: 'next_major'`, and `event` / `position` / `permissionSet` are unchanged.
   - The trigger predicate and the once-per-position cadence are unchanged.
   - **Hunks, seat-read:**
     - the `POSITION_NAME_FOLD_EVENT` docblock (~`:902-925`);
     - `reportNameFoldCollisions` and its docblock (~`:7005-7088`);
     - nothing near `computeControlledByParentFilter` or its call sites, which are seat 1's #24962 region.
   - **Pins:** 29 in `position-name-fold-warning.test.ts`. They include the exact payload keys and a pin that the grant itself is unchanged (a holder of `P` still resolves set `P`).
   - **Ablations** A1–A9 each went red as predicted and were restored to the HEAD blob `5db0a1f3c00a`. A8 is the 19.0 removal done early (5 red). A9 keeps the warning but drops the grant after it (4 red, on the grant assertion).
3. **Gates:**
   - CI on `e41097d233`, latest run per check name: 41 checks, 34 success, 7 skipped, 0 failed. Every skip is on the roster in `scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs` (read from the file): the 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate and Temporal Conformance. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are both `success`.
   - Local: 69 derived; 67 exit 0; 2 NOT-MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`: exit 3, prerequisite dists absent; CI runs both).
   - The `plugin-security` suite: 197 files, 4078 passed. Typecheck and `check:test-typecheck` exit 0.
4. **Accepted deviations:**
   - The suite and typecheck ran at `63246cedf`, before a one-commit merge of `origin/main` that touched only `plugin-approvals`. CI's run on this head is the reading of record.
   - No explain text changed: 「甲」 lists an explain line among the loud-half forms, but triage's derivation names only the warning, and `explain-engine.ts` was fenced.
   - The warning's provenance (17.3) is cited from the package CHANGELOG, because the checkout is shallow.
   - Prose read sentence by sentence against the diff and the cited code: the changeset's what-it-was / what-changed / why-only-a-warning / unchanged / what-to-do bullets, and the warning text itself.
5. **Out of scope:**
   - **Carried by #24757's 19.0 half, which removes this warning (noted, not filed):**
     - The warning's dedupe keys on the position name alone, so on a multi-organization deployment a second organization's undeclared pair `P` is not reported until restart once another organization's `P` has warned.
     - The warning is lazy (first resolution, never at boot), so a deployment where no holder of `P` has made a request has not been told.
   - **Acceptance notes, carrier none:** the `nameFoldWarned` docblock links `{@link reportNameFoldCollision}` (singular), which names no member. It is outside the claimed regions.
6. **Landing:** ordinary queue landing. Every check on this head is green or an expected skip, so the seat flips it (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`) on this record.
   - After the merge, #24757 moves to `pm:on-hold`, with `Restart-when:` the 19.0 line, for the fold's retirement.
   - The HotCRM half is objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2200, which the `repo:hotcrm` lane carries.
